# Commit 2

This homework was completed using R [@R]. The tidyverse package [@tidyverse] provides tools for data manipulation and visualization, while the knitr package [@knitr] was used for reproducible reporting.

We read an article by @Nese2022, which examined the growth and predictive performance of oral reading fluency measures. Two other articles were published in the same journal. One examined racial-ethnic inequality in school access [@Speroni2026] and another investigated ethnic-racial identity projects in Brazil [@Callegari2026].

# Commit 3

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

star |>
  group_by(sex, frl) |>
  summarize(
    math_mean = mean(tmathss, na.rm = TRUE),
    math_sd = sd(tmathss, na.rm = TRUE),
    rdg_mean = mean(treadss, na.rm = TRUE),
    rdg_sd = sd(treadss, na.rm = TRUE),
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

The table shows the mean and standard deviation of math and reading scores by sex and FRL status

# Commit 4

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

star |>
  ggplot(aes(x = totexp, y = tmathss)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, color = "gray70") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", aes(color=frl)) +
  labs(title = "Relation between teacher experience and math scores",
       subtitle = "Separate regression lines displayed by free/reduced price lunch status",
       x = "Teacher Experience (years)", 
       y = "Total Math Scale Score",
       color = "Lunch status") +
  scale_color_discrete(
    breaks = c("yes", "no"),
    labels = c("yes" = "Free/Reduced Price Meals", "no" = "Paid Meals"))+
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend)
```

The plot shows the relationship between teacher experience and math scores, with separate linear regression lines for students from families of different income levels (as indicated by their lunch status: receiving free/reduced price meals or not). The slopes for both regression lines are similarly positive, indicating that teacher experience has a comparable positive effect on math scores regardless of their household income condition. However, students coming from lower-income families (receiving free/reduced price meals) tend to have lower math scores overall compared to their peers who do not receive free/reduced price meals.
